description: The single-file molecule.yml, version 0.2.0: run defaults, a platform catalog, and a tree of scenarios. It describes how existing molecule scenario files appear in single-file form. Node config is molecule's own scenario schema (molecule.json), referenced rather than restated.

rules: Root = node with no parent. Every `scenarios` entry is a root.
Edge: nesting under `children:`. One parent per child.
A bare key applies to that node only and never cascades.
A key under the top-level `defaults:` applies to every node that does not set it bare.
K in the precedence is a key path, not a top-level key.
Mappings deep-merge across the precedence layers.
A list replaces the lower layer's list whole.
A null or empty-string value is an ordinary value.
The run is the virtual root: run-only keys bare, all cascading config under the top-level `defaults:`.
A `defaults:` block is a sparse overlay: any subset of config keys, none required. It is not a complete scenario.
`playbooks:` is a top-level convenience alias for `provisioner.playbooks`, valid wherever config is (bare, or under `defaults:`).
A `playbooks` value is a file path.
A relative `playbooks` path resolves against the node's scenario directory, `<scenarios directory>/<name>/`.
A stage the node leaves unset is found in the node's scenario directory by molecule's default discovery.
The FQCN playbook form (`design/data/layout.yml`) depends on molecule#4244, which is unmerged, so it is outside this version.
`platforms` is permissive: absent/empty is valid. Consumed only by a creating node, ignored otherwise.
The top-level `platforms:` is the catalog, and each entry defines one platform once by `name` with opaque `vars`.
A scenario's `platforms:` is a selection of catalog names, or inline platform objects for backward compatibility.
A root scenario with no `platforms:` selects the whole catalog. A child selects none of its own and inherits the parent's shared inventory.
Creation stays on the node, whose `playbooks.create` stands up the selected platforms and consumes their `vars`. The catalog dedups definition, not creation.
An inline platform object keeps its `name` exactly as written, as in molecule today.
A catalog selection's instance name is derived from the catalog name plus the scenario and run identity (`design/data/open-questions.yml`).
A catalog name and an inline platform name that match in one run is an error.
A child shares its parent's instances, beginning from the parent's inventory (`design/data/tree-spec.yml`).
A child whose parent is not standing has the parent created first (`design/data/tree-spec.yml`).
Sharing is within a tree only. There is no cross-tree share.
A key this schema does not declare fails validation, at every level.
Reserved/intrinsic names are clear of molecule's top-level keys. Near-misses (not collisions): `scenario` vs `scenarios`, and molecule's `shared_state`, which is not a key in this file.

platforms.description: The platform catalog. Each entry defines one platform once by name, with opaque creation vars. A scenario selects catalog entries by name.

defaults.description: Config for the run and everything below it. A sparse overlay of molecule scenario keys.

scenarios.description: Root nodes. Run in wave order, and top-to-bottom in list order within a wave (serial order, scheduler submit order).

catalogPlatform.description: A catalog platform definition. Names a platform once so scenarios select it by name, with opaque creation vars. Creation stays on the node in this surface, so no create playbook lives here.

name.description: Catalog identity, referenced by a scenario's `platforms` list. Unique across the catalog.

vars.description: Opaque creation vars passed through to the create step. Molecule holds no knowledge of them.

platformSelection.description: A scenario's platform set: catalog names as strings, or inline platform objects (backward compatible). Absent on a root selects the whole catalog.

playbooks.description: One playbook path per stage. A relative path resolves against the node's scenario directory.

create.description: Path to the playbook that creates the node's instances.

prepare.description: Path to the playbook that prepares the instances before converge.

converge.description: Path to the playbook that applies the content under test.

side_effect.description: Path to the playbook that applies a side effect before verify.

verify.description: Path to the playbook that verifies the instances.

cleanup.description: Path to the playbook that cleans up before destroy.

destroy.description: Path to the playbook that destroys the node's instances.

config.description: A sparse molecule scenario-config overlay: any subset of these keys, none required. Each value is validated by molecule's own per-key subschema (molecule.json).

playbooks.description: The `provisioner.playbooks` mapping, by file path (top-level alias). The FQCN form is outside this version. `create`/`destroy` bare by convention so a parent that creates does not hand creation to children.

driver.description: Typically bare on a creating node, so it is not handed to children.

platforms.description: Selection of catalog platform names, or inline platform objects. Consumed only by a node that creates its own instances.

node.description: A scenario as a member of a tree. Node-intrinsic keys, children, and any config key bare (this node only).

name.description: Node identity, selected by `-s`. Unique across the run.

wave.description: Ordering tier among nodes that share a parent (`design/data/scheduling.yml`).

children.description: Child nodes. The nesting is the parent edge (single-file mode). A child shares its parent's instances.
